clue.text: Heavy blow requiring doctor's injection in risky operation

indicators.note: an injection goes into a body, so the doctor's letters are put inside the heavy blow

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind, a heavy blow
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A patient needs a jab during a dangerous surgical procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' reads as a punch, but here it is a wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamble is a venture whose outcome is uncertain and could lose.

clue.text: Number supporting Church's militant group

parts.note: a number can be a song or tune, an air
to be for something is to support it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A hymn backing the idea of the Church Militant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure; it is a musical number.
explanation.definitionFit: An air force is a nation's military aviation arm, a fighting body.

clue.text: An important personage seen at the fairground

definitions.meaning: a VIP, a big shot in an organisation
a giant revolving ride with seats round its rim

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a powerful person, and also the name of the Ferris-wheel ride at funfairs.

clue.text: Worthy Eastern firm I am employed in

indicators.note: being employed in a place puts you inside it, so the letters go within

parts.note: firm in the sense of steady means stable
contracted to I'm

explanation.surface: A respectable eastern company where the speaker works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company; it is the adjective meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimable describes someone deserving esteem and respect.

clue.text: Drove fiercely and got runs, chary openers having settled in

indicators.note: settling in means taking up a place inside, so the letters sit within

parts.note: in cricket, getting runs is having scored

indicators.note: the opening letters of the word chary are taken

explanation.surface: A cricketer batted aggressively once the cautious opening batsmen had got their eye in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openers' is plural, so the first two letters of 'chary' are taken, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorched is old slang for driving or cycling at great speed.

clue.text: Repository for proceeds from Hitchcock tale, say

definitions.meaning: a bookkeeping account where money is held until its proper place is decided
a story by Hitchcock, the master of suspense, is a thriller narrative

explanation.definitionFit: In bookkeeping, an account holding uncertain sums; read whimsically it is a tale full of tension, as Hitchcock made.

clue.text: Took a rest after flight home?

definitions.text: Took a rest after flight home?

parts.words: Took a rest after flight home?
parts.note: reads as a weary traveller resting after flying home, but describes birds settling on a perch for the night

explanation.definitionFit: Birds that have flown back and settled on their perch for sleep have done this.

clue.text: Seditious leader held by chief executioner

indicators.note: something held by another is enclosed by it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a headman is a chief of a tribe or village

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word seditious is taken

explanation.surface: A rebel ringleader is captured by the top hangman.
explanation.definitionFit: A headsman was the official who beheaded condemned prisoners.

clue.text: Party men stage canvass

parts.note: a do is a party
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers
a step is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: Party members put on a campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvass' is a verb: to go door to door seeking votes.
explanation.definitionFit: To doorstep is to call on people at home, as political canvassers do.

clue.text: Ships appearing after half a day passes

indicators.note: the passes come after the half day in the answer

parts.note: the first half of Friday
gates are passes through a wall or fence

explanation.surface: Ships turn up after the gates have been open half a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half a day' means half of a day's name, FRI from FRIDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigates are a class of warship.

clue.text: Fish showing disturbance after perch is thrown back

indicators.note: the disturbance comes after the turned perch
thrown back means the word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a perch or rod is an old unit of length
ado is fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: An angler throws back a perch and causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' looks like a fish next to 'Fish', but it is the measure, a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: The dorado is a large game fish of warm seas, also called mahi-mahi.

clue.text: First person lodged in good French dwelling finding great companionship

parts.note: bon is French for good

indicators.note: lodging in a place means staying inside it, so the letter goes within

parts.note: a home is a dwelling
I is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: A lodger finds friendly company in a fine French house.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonhomie is cheerful friendliness and good fellowship.

clue.text: Secret police, source of support for unchanging state

parts.note: the Stasi were East Germany's secret police

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Secret police are the bedrock of a regime that never changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a condition of balance where nothing develops or alters.

clue.text: Did relief work after printing unit head meets editor

indicators.note: the head is placed after the printing unit

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of measure
a boss is a head or chief

explanation.surface: At a newspaper, the boss of the press room meets the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief work' suggests aid; here it is raised decoration on metal or leather.
explanation.definitionFit: To emboss is to carve or mould a design standing out in relief.

clue.text: Leader of riot with ideal organisation

indicators.note: organising the letters means rearranging them into a new order

explanation.surface: A riot's ringleader has a perfect plan for organising it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' is the newspaper sense: the main opinion article.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader in a newspaper is its editorial, the piece giving the paper's view.

clue.text: Instrument endlessly used in dungeon

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the instrument goes

parts.note: a cello is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A prisoner plays music non-stop in his dungeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is a small room for a prisoner, as in a dungeon.

clue.text: Extremely astute girl's received by court

indicators.note: something received by another is taken inside it

parts.note: Annie's, a girl's name with the possessive

explanation.surface: A very shrewd young woman is welcomed at court.
explanation.definitionFit: Canny means shrewd, so the superlative means shrewdest of all.

clue.text: Turning point in dock used by many an old vessel

parts.note: to dock a ship is to land it
M, the Roman thousand, stands for many
Noah's ark was an ancient boat

explanation.surface: A harbour used by plenty of old ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A landmark is an event marking a significant change in history.

clue.text: Holds back to get a bargain

indicators.note: back means the word is turned to read from right to left

parts.note: a wrestler pins an opponent, holding them down

explanation.surface: Someone restrains themselves to pick up a cheap deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is British slang for something bought cheaply.

clue.text: Seated initially on mount that's most testing

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word seated

parts.note: Mount Everest, the world's highest mountain

explanation.surface: Sitting on top of the hardest mountain of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Severest means harshest or most demanding.

clue.text: Popular ticket readily available

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a season is short for a season ticket

explanation.surface: A sought-after ticket can be had easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Food in season is plentiful because it is at its natural time of harvest.

clue.text: Punish lapse in English composition

indicators.note: composing letters means putting them together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A teacher marks down a slip in an English essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' looks like a school essay; it signals rearranging LAPSE, IN and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To penalise is to impose a penalty on someone.

clue.text: The best drink improves one's health

parts.note: the pick of something is the best of it
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: The finest tonic restores you.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rallies after illness is said to be recovering in this way.

clue.text: Make a mistake, leading diamonds without any prospect of success

indicators.note: the mistake comes first, leading the diamonds

parts.note: to nod is to slip up, as in Homer nods
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player errs by leading diamonds, a hopeless play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds' looks like a card suit; it is jewellery slang.
explanation.definitionFit: No dice is an informal phrase meaning no chance, nothing doing.

clue.text: Friendly chap shut away in small room

parts.note: close friends are friendly
Ted, a man's name

explanation.surface: An amiable fellow is locked in a tiny room.
explanation.definitionFit: Closeted means hidden away in private, as if in a cupboard.

clue.text: Turning — please pass

indicators.note: turning the letters about means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone at a junction politely asks to be let through.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes by.

clue.text: Creation from a Parisian individual having several lines in collection

parts.note: un is French for a
I, one, is an individual
a verse is a group of lines of poetry gathered together

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's anthology of poems.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is all of creation, everything that exists.

clue.text: Join the company in appropriate role

definitions.meaning: an actor joining the theatre company in a suitable acting role

explanation.definitionFit: To take part is to participate, and also, read literally, an actor accepting a role.

clue.text: Landed with some tedious recital

parts.note: lit, past tense of light, means landed or alighted
any means some

explanation.surface: A dull speech came with the arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a long repetitive list, from the repeated petitions of church prayer.
